name: Vieille Ville
description: Colmar's historic old town, a compact web of half-timbered houses, cobbled lanes and squares around the Collegiale Saint-Martin. Museums, shops and restaurants cluster here, making it the most scenic and walkable base, though also the busiest with visitors.
bestFor: Travellers wanting storybook streets and sights on foot

name: Petite Venise
description: The Little Venice quarter along the Lauch river, famous for its flower-lined canals and pastel houses. Part of the old town's southern edge, it is intensely photogenic, with the covered market and waterside restaurants drawing crowds year-round.
bestFor: Short-stay visitors seeking canals, photos and charm

name: Gare and Sud
description: The area around Colmar's railway station, southwest of the old town. More modern and everyday, it offers hotels, supermarkets and rail links to Strasbourg and beyond, with lower prices and an easy walk into the historic centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting rail links and better value rooms

name: Champ de Mars and North
tagline: Green residential streets by the park
description: The residential quarter north of the centre around the Champ de Mars park, Colmar's largest green space. Calm tree-lined streets and apartment blocks make it quieter and more local, with the old town a short, pleasant walk away.
bestFor: Remote workers wanting quiet, green, walkable residential streets
